title: A reused data set or --case-basis run is compared with a database record that binds a different PP/NAO/ABFS
symptom: A LibRPA-only rerun on an existing BN data set produced a GW gap of 6.12 eV while the bn-paper-sg15 record reports 6.32 eV. The case data used a 2s2p1d NAO and no prebuilt ABFS, while the record binds B/N-SG15 (3s3p2d NAO, pca1e-6 ABFS). The 0.20 eV difference is a basis difference, not a LibRPA setting difference.
root_cause: The run was launched with --case-basis and --policy-mode replay. --case-basis disabled database staging, and replay skipped the production-only basis_source/kpoint gates. No gate hashed the payloads that were actually used, so a declared basis was mistaken for evidence of the basis used.
minimal_fix: Before any compute, run scripts/verify_case_inputs.py --case <dir> --basis-root <LibRPA-database> --basis-family SG15. It hashes every PP/NAO/ABFS on disk and compares it with the element set bound to the reference record. If the case binds a different set, regenerate the DFT data with the database payloads (or do not compare with that record). The loop now runs policy.basis_identity, which fails on a mismatch in every mode, including replay.
validation: The verifier on bn-k222-sym-v1-shrink-head-g0w0 reports B/N NAO mismatches and missing ABFS, and reports the case shrink_abfs_pca_thr=0.1 as below the 1e-4 standard. A database-aligned bundle must report match=yes for every element/role before submission.
avoid: Do not use --case-basis for a run that will be compared with a database reference. Do not use --policy-mode replay for new physical compute. Do not treat a declared basis, a STRU element name, or a matching pseudopotential as evidence that the NAO/ABFS match; only the hashes of the files actually read are evidence.
